summary: In the temple, Jesus calls Himself the light of the world and finally says, “Before Abraham was, I AM,” and His hearers take up stones.
key_insight: Twice Jesus says “I am He” (8:24, 28); in Greek it is simply “I am.” The crowd did not grasp it until He said, “Before Abraham was, I AM.” Then they understood Him to be taking the name God gave at the burning bush (Exodus 3:14), and they picked up stones.
story: Teaching in the treasury of the temple, Jesus spoke to the people again: “I am the light of the world. He who follows Me shall not walk in darkness, but have the light of life.” The Pharisees objected, “You bear witness of Yourself; Your witness is not true.” Jesus answered that His witness was true, because He knew where He came from and where He was going, and the Father who sent Him bore witness too. “Where is Your Father?” they asked. “You know neither Me nor My Father,” He said. Still no one laid hands on Him, for His hour had not yet come.

Then He warned them, “I am going away, and you will seek Me, and will die in your sin. Where I go you cannot come.” They wondered aloud whether He meant to kill Himself. “You are from beneath; I am from above,” He said. “If you do not believe that I am He, you will die in your sins.” When they asked, “Who are You?” He said He was just what He had told them from the beginning, and added, “When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He.” As He spoke these words, many believed in Him.

To those who had believed Him, Jesus said, “If you abide in My word, you are My disciples indeed. And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” They answered, “We are Abraham’s descendants, and have never been in bondage to anyone.” Jesus replied, “Most assuredly, I say to you, whoever commits sin is a slave of sin.” Only the Son could set them free: “Therefore if the Son makes you free, you shall be free indeed.”

The argument grew sharper. They claimed Abraham as their father, and Jesus said Abraham’s children would do Abraham’s works, not seek to kill a Man who told them the truth. They claimed God as their Father, and Jesus said, “If God were your Father, you would love Me.” He told them plainly that their desires came from their father the devil, a murderer and a liar from the beginning. Then He asked, “Which of you convicts Me of sin?”

They answered with insults: “Do we not say rightly that You are a Samaritan and have a demon?” Jesus said He honored His Father and did not seek His own glory. “Most assuredly, I say to you, if anyone keeps My word he shall never see death.” Now they were sure He had a demon. Abraham was dead, and the prophets too. “Are You greater than our father Abraham, who is dead?”

Jesus answered, “Your father Abraham rejoiced to see My day, and he saw it and was glad.” They said, “You are not yet fifty years old, and have You seen Abraham?” Jesus said to them, “Most assuredly, I say to you, before Abraham was, I AM.”
Then they took up stones to throw at Him. But Jesus hid Himself and went out of the temple, passing through the midst of them.

scene.label: The treasury
scene.text: John places this teaching “in the treasury” (8:20). The offering chests stood in the Court of Women (compare Mark 12:41), one of the busiest places in the temple, open to every Israelite man and woman.

scene.label: Lamps of the feast
scene.text: Later Jewish writings describe huge golden lampstands lit in the Court of Women during the Feast of Tabernacles, so bright that they lit up the city’s courtyards. Jesus spoke these words at the close of that feast or soon after, probably in the same court.

scene.label: Light in Israel’s story
scene.text: God led Israel through the wilderness by a pillar of fire at night (Exodus 13:21). Isaiah promised that people walking in darkness would see a great light (Isaiah 9:2), and that God’s Servant would be “a light to the Gentiles” (Isaiah 49:6).

scene.label: Two witnesses
scene.text: The law required two or three witnesses to establish a matter (Deuteronomy 19:15). Jesus names His two: Himself, and the Father who sent Him.

scene.label: “I AM”
scene.text: God gave His name to Moses as “I AM WHO I AM” (Exodus 3:14), and through Isaiah He said, “Indeed before the day was, I am He” (Isaiah 43:13). The law punished blasphemy by stoning (Leviticus 24:16).

witnesses.john: Only John records this exchange, part of his account of Jesus at the Jerusalem feasts, where the conflict with the leaders comes into the open. The chapter climbs from “I am the light of the world” to “before Abraham was, I AM,” in line with John’s stated purpose: that readers may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God (20:31).

seeing.reveals: Jesus claims to be the light of the world, the Son sent from above, and the eternal I AM who existed before Abraham. He does not soften the claim, even when it costs Him the crowd.
seeing.living: Jesus spoke His hardest words to people who had just “believed Him” (8:31). Faith that lasts abides in His word and lets His truth name the sin that enslaves. Follow Him, and you will not walk in darkness.
seeing.ponder: Where are you still calling yourself free while Jesus calls it slavery?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus is the eternal I AM; following Him is the only way out of darkness and slavery.
outline: The Son who must be believed (21–30)
preaching.watch_for: The sharpest words in the chapter (v. 44) are spoken to people who had just believed Him (v. 31). John shows that belief which will not abide in Jesus’ word can turn, within one conversation, to picking up stones (v. 59).
